name: X.Plosion
caption: Took CCW's World Heavyweight Championship from its first champion, Desmond Harrison, at FanFest, and beat him again to keep it on the fed's first RSPWF broadcast.

tenures.role: wrestler — CCW World Heavyweight Champion (1 reign)
tenures.source: The fed's own "Explosion!!" PPV promo (in the World title tournament); the fed's own RSPWF-debut promo and "CCW Slamfest" show script (won the title from Desmond Harrison at FanFest; retained it in the Slamfest main event).

identity.note: Shares a name with euwc-x-plosion (EUWC's own World/International Champion, 1996-97) — same era, no shared operator, roster, or crossover document found; a bare name/era match is not evidence of a join under the identity-join test, so this stays distinct pending any actual corroboration.

name: Desmond Harrison
caption: CCW's first World Heavyweight Champion, crowned in the 8-man Explosion!! tournament; he lost the belt to X.Plosion at FanFest and came up short in the rematch on the fed's first RSPWF broadcast.

tenures.role: wrestler — CCW World Heavyweight Champion (1 reign, the first); 1997 title challenger
tenures.source: The fed's own "First Night" card announcement (r4zfr6TQsp4J; First Night, 18 January 1997, where Slamfest recalls his win over Bradley Warden); the fed's own "Explosion!!" PPV promo (in the World title tournament that crowned the first champion); the fed's own RSPWF-debut promo (former World Champion); the fed's own "CCW Slamfest" show script (title challenger, main event); the fed's own card of 1 February 2001 ("the man who first held the CCW World Title").

name: "Boardwalk" Bradley Warden
caption: CCW's own first-ever International Champion, who went on to become NCCW's own president under his own out-of-character name a season later.

tenures.role: wrestler — CCW International Champion (2 reigns, the first champion)
tenures.source: The fed's own "First Night" card announcement (r4zfr6TQsp4J; against Desmond Harrison at First Night, 18 January 1997); the fed's own "Explosion!!" PPV promo (became the first International Champion by pinning Ricky Revolution; billed to defend against him at Explosion!!); the fed's own "CCW Slamfest" show script (won the title back from Ricky Revolution, billed "2-Time CCW International Champion"; non-title win over Bill MacRagge).

name: Bill "The Ironman" MacRagge
caption: A CCW West Coast Championship challenger who lost a hard-fought non-title match to the fed's own International Champion on its first RSPWF broadcast.

tenures.source: The fed's own "Explosion!!" PPV promo; the fed's own "CCW Slamfest" show script (non-title loss to Bradley Warden).

name: "Sensational" Sean Watts
caption: Won CCW's rookie contest on the fed's first RSPWF broadcast by twisting his opponent's nose for the submission.

tenures.source: The fed's own "CCW Slamfest" show script.

name: "Crippler" Jimmy Payne
caption: Lost CCW's rookie contest on the fed's first RSPWF broadcast to "Sensational" Sean Watts.

tenures.source: The fed's own "CCW Slamfest" show script.

name: "The Bullet" Ricky Revolution
caption: A former CCW International Championship challenger who earned a future West Coast Championship shot by beating "IQ" Ian Quartz on the fed's first RSPWF broadcast.

tenures.role: wrestler — CCW International Champion (1 reign); earned a West Coast Championship shot
tenures.source: The fed's own "First Night" card announcement (r4zfr6TQsp4J; the West Coast Championship tournament at First Night, 18 January 1997, where the Explosion!! promo's footage shows him pinned by "GQ" Geoffrey Quartz for the title); the fed's own "Explosion!!" PPV promo (International Championship challenger); the fed's own "CCW Slamfest" show script (former International Champion; non-title win over Ian Quartz).

identity.note: Merged with the FASW wing's ricky-revolution-fasw-1997 (coordinator ruling 2026-09-04): identical billed name with nickname, FASW's own 10 May 1997 press-conference text names Classic Championship Wrestling as his prior fed, contiguous 1997 dates. The FASW id is retired to an alias; its tenure is carried here. (the retired id ricky-revolution-fasw-1997 now aliases here; validate resolves `with` against live ids only)

name: "IQ" Ian Quartz
caption: Held the CCW West Coast Championship into the fed's first RSPWF broadcast, where he lost a non-title match to "The Bullet" Ricky Revolution and a future title shot.

tenures.role: wrestler — CCW West Coast Champion (1 reign)
tenures.source: The fed's own "Explosion!!" PPV promo (eliminated his brother GQ from a battle royal to enter the World title tournament); the fed's own "CCW Slamfest" show script (won the West Coast title from GQ at FanFest; non-title loss to Ricky Revolution).

name: "GQ" Geoffrey Quartz
caption: Won CCW's first-ever West Coast Championship at the fed's own "First Night" debut show before later resurfacing as a wrestler in the record's own successor fed, NCCW.

tenures.role: wrestler — CCW West Coast Champion (1 reign, the first)
tenures.source: The fed's own RSPWF-debut promo ("the former CCW West Coast Champion 'GQ' Geoffrey Quartz, just after he won the title at First Night"); the fed's own "Explosion!!" PPV promo (pinning Ricky Revolution for the title; billed to defend it against Bill MacRagge); the fed's own "CCW Slamfest" show script (lost the title to his brother Ian at FanFest).

The fed's own titles page (promotions/nccw-1998/archive/nccw-titles-1999.html). Won the International Championship 27 May 1998 (NCCW Superstars Live); co-won the World Tag Team Championship with Don Cameron 26 August 1998 (a tournament final, Denver Coliseum). The fed's own Battle in Seattle results page, 7 August 1999 (promotions/nccw-1998/archive/nccw-battle-in-seattle-1999-08-07.html). Defeated "Delinquent" Kevin Fontaine on the undercard.

tenures.role: wrestler, billed "GQ" Geoffery Quartz; President Cameron's former NCCW tag team partner
tenures.note: The card has him mouth "I made this fed"; the fed's own commentary calls him Mr. CCW.

name: Curt Crane
caption: CCW's own co-founder and co-president, who also wrestled and hosted under his own name before resurfacing as NCCW's own "StarFox" Curt Crane a season later.

tenures.source: The fed's own recruitment ads and founding statement (self-signed co-president); the fed's own "Explosion!!" PPV promo (hosts "Fox's Den", billed ICW Wrestler of the Year).

tenures.note: Accepted the ICW "Wrestler of the Year" award for 1996 on air, recapping his win of the ICW World Heavyweight Title at the "ICW Blood Bowl" tournament, then immediately challenged Chris Scott for the Light-Heavyweight/Cruiserweight title; billed as a member of the Phoenix Squad alongside Brian Anthony and manager Fara Phoenix.

name: David Lombardi
caption: CCW's own in-fiction president, credited on-air with signing and pulling matches for the fed's first RSPWF broadcast.

tenures.source: The fed's own "CCW Slamfest" show script.

name: Jack Maverick
caption: Went to a double count-out with "Shotgun" Gage Thompson in Washington, DC, then beat Steve Johnson with the Path Less Traveled to reach the 2001 CCW World Title tournament.

name: "The Grey Wolf" Marc Denis
caption: Half of Les Canadians, who announced his retirement and then wrestled one last match in Washington, DC, lost to Lew Spectre's Star Island Stranglehold.

name: Rex Reagan
caption: Threw Brian Anthony off the scaffold in Washington, DC, and with Shakes Reagan beat Fire & Ice in Florida a week later.

name: Shakes Reagan
caption: The smaller in-ring member of the Reagans, thrown off the scaffold by Gage Thompson in Washington, DC, and the man who pinned Alex Perkins for the team's win over Fire & Ice.

name: Duff Reagan
caption: The largest of the Reagans, one of President Don Cameron's enforcers on both of the fed's surviving 2001 cards.

name: Underpants Reagan
caption: The fourth Reagan, named the CCW's Vice President by President Don Cameron on the card of 1 February 2001.

name: Chris Kanne
aka: "The Man of a Million Holds" Chris Kanne

tenures.role: the CCW's Enforcer, guest referee and, by his own word, a CCW original

caption: "The Man of a Million Holds", billed in the fed's 1997 promotion and its Enforcer in 2001, until he stun-gunned Lew Spectre and Jim Sergeant and was fired.

name: Todd Fischer
caption: Lead commentator on the fed's 1997 broadcast and again on its January 2001 card, before a suspension kept him off the next.

name: "Suave" Stevie West
caption: Commentator on the fed's 1997 broadcast and on both of its surviving 2001 cards.

name: Michael Garrison
caption: Ring announcer on the fed's 1997 broadcast and on both of its surviving 2001 cards.

name: Robert Flamingo
caption: The fed's journalist and interviewer in 1997 and again on both of its surviving 2001 cards.

name: Mr. Darksey
caption: Backstage interviewer on the January 2001 card, interrupted when Superstar attacked Ryan Douglas.
